title: Deferred cell rendering and pressure-sensitive resize affordance
creator: Aisha Morgan
description:
Problem: Complex pages with many virtualized rows and rich cell renderers (avatars, charts, badges) are causing jank during scroll and slow initial render when opening large lists. Meanwhile, designers want a more discoverable and forgiving column resize interaction that feels precise on both mouse and touch.

Goal: Implement a deferred cell-rendering strategy for the table component, plus a new resize affordance that adapts to input velocity/pressure (simulated on devices that lack force input) to allow fast coarse adjustments and precise fine adjustments. Ensure keyboard accessibility, persistent column widths, and minimal visual shift for users.

Scope: design tokens/visuals for skeletons, resize handle states, interaction specs for drag/long-press/keyboard, ARIA patterns, and handoff artifacts for ENG-4021 and ENG-4102 to implement runtime changes and perf heuristics.
acceptance_criteria: Table renders placeholder skeletons for offscreen cells and progressively hydrates visible cells within 30–50ms of becoming visible
CPU work on initial mount for pages with 10k rows is reduced by at least 30% in our synthetic benchmark
Resize affordance supports: quick-drag (coarse), slow-drag (fine), long-press + drag (precision mode), and keyboard controls with +/- by 1px and 10px increments
Accessible labels and instructions exist for screen reader users (announce mode: 'resize column' and current width in pixels), and compatibility with high-contrast themes
Column width changes persist per-user (local storage) and are included in the per-route layout export API
Design sign-off from PM and Engineering and a QA checklist passing on Chrome, Safari, Firefox, and latest iPadOS
No regressions in existing virtualization tests; visual snapshot coverage added for skeleton state and resize handle focus styles
design_notes:
Proposed visuals: neutral gray skeletons with staggered shimmer for deferred cells; resize handle expands to a 10px hit area on hover/focus while visually staying 2px. Introduce a micromotion for precision mode (long-press) that slightly enlarges the handle and displays a pixel ruler tooltip. Use tokens: token-size-border, token-color-skeleton, token-elevation-overlay.

Interaction heuristics: measure drag velocity over the first 80ms -> if velocity > threshold switch to coarse multiplier (e.g., drag 10px -> width change 40px); if velocity low or long-press active, apply fine multiplier (drag 1px -> 1px). For touch/stylus, interpret touch force via PointerEvent.pressure when available; fallback to long-press + small movement.

Accessibility: keyboard: focus handle with Tab, ArrowLeft/ArrowRight adjust by 1px, Shift+Arrow by 10px, Alt+Arrow snaps to default/fitted width. Announce 'Column Name, width 240 pixels' on change. Documented in ARIA pattern doc and included in design tokens guidance.
engineering_notes:
Hand-off items for ENG: runtime hooks for deferred render queue, intersection-observer thresholds tuned to row height distribution, and an experimental 'fast-path' for simple cell renderers (strings, numbers, chips) that skip hydration. Provide a ResizeController API that emits coarse/fine mode and velocity values.

Potential trade-offs: deferred rendering increases first interaction latency for offscreen-to-onscreen rows if the hydration budget is too low; will add a progressive budget slot to allow immediate hydration for a few cells on sudden scroll stops. Persisted widths stored in localStorage key 'rdw_table_layout_v2' with migration from old key.

Links: Figma: https://figma.com/file/ABC123/table-deferred-and-resize, PR stub: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood-ui/pull/8921, perf benchmark: https://dashboard.internal/redwood/perf/tables/2026-02
qa_plan:
1) Verify skeletons display and hydrate when scrolled into view; 2) Run synthetic perf suite comparing mount/memory with and without deferred rendering; 3) Test resize interactions across input types: mouse, touch, stylus, keyboard; 4) Accessibility audit with NVDA and VoiceOver for announcements and focus order; 5) Visual regression snapshots for handle hover/focus/active and skeleton states.

Test matrix: Chrome/Windows, Safari/macOS, Firefox/Ubuntu, iPadOS Safari (touch).
checklist: Finalize token names and add to design-tokens repo
Prototype in Figma and validate micro-interactions
Engineer: implement ResizeController API and persistence
Add unit and e2e tests for hydration and resize modes
Ship behind feature flag and rollout via canary
